concerns.text: FR-006 mandates the system 'enforce a memory usage limit of ≤7 GB... automatically sampling or subsetting data if necessary'. Plan Phase 1 assigns memory_monitor.py this adaptive subsetting fallback, but no task builds or tests it — T008 only *records* peak RAM via memory_monitor.py. The enforcement mechanism (streaming, deterministic seeded subsetting, hard abort) is a dropped plan constraint; add a task (or extend T004/T008) that implements and unit-tests the adaptive fallback.

US-3 acceptance scenario 1 requires the correlation analysis to 'complete within 5 minutes'. T006's verification (test_correlation.py, test_sensitivity.py) checks rows and flag logic but no task verifies this runtime bound; SC-004/T008 cover only the 6-hour whole-pipeline limit. The acceptance criterion is silently dropped — add a timed assertion or record the correlation-stage runtime in verification_run_summary.csv.

Spec FR-005 and US-3 sweep the significance *p*-value threshold; T006 sweeps FDR-corrected *q* ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}. The plan has the same drift. Counts differ between interpretations; either reconcile the spec wording via kickback or have T006 explicitly document that q-thresholds are the implemented reading of FR-005.

FR-011 unconditionally requires real-data validation; the tasks defer it behind the plan's re-plan trigger, which the spec does not authorize. The deferral is documented honestly (not silent), so this is not a weakening by the task list itself — but the spec needs an explicit conditional/deferred clause mirroring FR-001's, or the delivered work will contradict the spec as written. Keep the kickback flag active; do not let T007's machinery validation be read as FR-011 satisfaction (T007 currently states this correctly).
